canonical_statement: The study aimed to compare the clinical and metabolic effectiveness of empagliflozin with dapagliflozin and DPP-4 inhibitors in patients with type 2 diabetes treated in routine clinical practice using the nationwide Korean NHIS database.

canonical_statement: Baseline covariates included age, sex, income quintile, diabetes duration, hypertension, dyslipidemia, ASCVD, CKD, chronic diabetic complications, prior hypoglycemia/DKA/UTI, metformin, insulin, RAAS-inhibitor and statin use, plus baseline fasting glucose, eGFR, and BMI.

canonical_statement: Matching used 1:1 nearest-neighbor matching without replacement via a greedy algorithm with a caliper of 0.2 standard deviations of the logit propensity score.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: One-to-one nearest-neighbor matching without replacement was performed using a greedy algorithm with a caliper width of 0.2 standard deviations of the logit of the propensity score.

canonical_statement: Standardized mean differences below 0.10 were considered adequate covariate balance.

canonical_statement: Clinical outcomes were analyzed in matched cohorts using Cox proportional-hazards models to estimate hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals.

canonical_statement: Outcome models were additionally adjusted for baseline covariates after matching as a doubly robust approach.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The outcome models were additionally adjusted for baseline covariates to minimize residual confounding (doubly robust approach).

canonical_statement: Laboratory outcomes used linear mixed-effects models with fixed effects for group, time, and group-by-time interaction, compound-symmetry covariance, and Kenward–Roger degrees of freedom.
